newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to announce new rouble denomination.
newsitem.headline: Russia to announce new rouble denomination.

text.p: Russia is to announce a new rouble denomination on Monday, central bank spokesman Alexei Sitnin said on Monday.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin was expected to make an announcement on the new denomination at noon local time (0800 GMT) on Monday.

Sitnin declined to say what form the redenomination would take, but sources in the central bank said it was likely to slash three zeros from rouble banknotes. They did not say over what period the changes would take place.
Russian inflation soared in the early 1990s as the former planned economy was disbanded, reaching an annual rate of over 1,000 percent in September and October 1993.
It has fallen steadily since, with the consumer price index increase dropping to an annual 14.5 percent in June, the last month for which year-on-year data is available.
The highest denominated banknote in Russia is 500,000 roubles, which was introduced in March. At current exchange rates it is worth just $86.
In Soviet time the rouble was pegged at an artificial rate of 0.55 to the dollar. The 500,000 rouble banknote would theoretically have been worth over $900,000.
